data.text: NickNameChanger 0.0.18 is available for Hytale 0.6.x, built against server 0.6.8. It fixes nickname commands, keeps real usernames unchanged for other mods, and adds chat adapters for mini-chat-formatter 0.1.x, EssentialsPlus and EliteEssentials. It also adds nickname rules, a separate message-color permission and automatic config migration. See the description for each chat plugin's setup and limits. Use /nnc if another mod owns /nick. The name at the top of the inventory or character screen comes from the game client and your account. No server mod can change it. I don't read CurseForge comments. Please report bugs on GitHub Issues: https://github.com/UberMorgott/Hytale-Mod-NickNameChanger/issues

replies.text: In 0.0.18, you can use NNC with LuckPerms alone. NNC formats chat and reads LP prefixes and suffixes. If you prefer mini-chat-formatter, the adapter supports 0.1.x: keep its username tag for the nickname and its message tag for message colors. That setup does not need PlaceholderAPI. For old LuckPerms 5.5.28 betas with a built-in formatter, set chat-formatter.enabled to false. Use one chat formatter and check the startup log's "Integrations:" line to see what NNC detected. I don't read CurseForge comments, so please report future bugs on GitHub Issues: https://github.com/UberMorgott/Hytale-Mod-NickNameChanger/issues

replies.text:
In reply to user_qboulv2w800ky8wl: Hey, glad you like the mod! Unfortunately, this isn't something I can easily fix right now. The inventory UI is part of the game client and loads before any mods do, so there's no clean way to modify it from a regular mod.
 
There is a way to do it — essentially patching the client's memory at runtime, similar to how Cheat Engine works — but that would require turning this into an "early plugin" mod, which is a completely different beast. It wouldn't work with the mod manager, would be much harder to install, and honestly starts to feel more like game hacking than modding. Not something I want to go down that road with.
 
For now, we're just waiting on better tools that give mods proper access to the client-side UI. Once that's available, this will definitely be doable. Fingers crossed!

replies.text: 0.0.18 adds migration for old config keys and fixes LP prefix formatting. When migration is needed, the original config is saved as config.json.pre-0.0.18.bak. Unreadable nickname files are no longer overwritten, and failed saves show an error. This cannot recover nicknames already lost; those need an existing backup. Your separate message-color permission is also in this release. Use /lp group default permission set nickname.msgcolor false to block message colors while keeping nickname colors. I don't read CurseForge comments, so please report future bugs on GitHub Issues: https://github.com/UberMorgott/Hytale-Mod-NickNameChanger/issues

In reply to Statboy: Hey! The mod went through a pretty significant rework in the last update, and the file format used to store nicknames and prefixes likely changed as a result — that's probably why everything got reset. It was a compatibility-related change, sorry for the inconvenience!
 
Could you let me know if newly assigned names and prefixes are saving correctly now? That would help me figure out if this is just a one-time reset or an ongoing issue.

replies.text: 0.0.18 adds an adapter for mini-chat-formatter 0.1.x. Its username tag shows the nickname and its message tag gets the message color. Its LP tags remain in place. NNC's own LP prefix parser also handles scoped colors and gradients. For map-only nicknames, enable Display.ShowOnMap and disable ShowInChat, ShowOnNameplate and ShowInTabList under Display. Map labels use plain text, without chat colors. I don't read CurseForge comments, so please report future bugs on GitHub Issues: https://github.com/UberMorgott/Hytale-Mod-NickNameChanger/issues

replies.text: v0.0.15 includes Mini-Chat-Formatter compatibility improvements. However, we've confirmed that MCF itself has a version incompatibility with the current Hytale server — it doesn't format chat even without NNC installed. Once MCF releases an updated version, NNC should work seamlessly with it. In the meantime, NNC works great standalone with LuckPerms or with EssentialsPlus.
